closed-mode-plan.text: The story, the requirements and the rulings are in the closed mode specification. This page records the class of the change, the shape of the code, the order of work, the invariants and the hosted checks that accept it. Issue 654, one pull request, one slice, about four hours of writing. Base: main cfe78df1. It lands after issue 651 (the blueprint title it consumes) and is merged by Saturday 17 October 09:00 UTC.

class-and-team.text: The change adds behaviour to the open-datum executable: a flag, a read of the chain, and a refusal. It takes the full process. One commit owner writes the slice. A persistent auditor, silent toward the writer, answers the checkpoints. One independent gate author wrote a table of hosted checks before any coding, and the author of this plan combined it with a table of their own, once. Draft tool: none. No part of the change is Lean, on-chain code or a workflow.

how-a-command-finds-its-mode.text: How a command finds its mode.

When the mode cannot be read, the command runs as open-datum. This is safe because the command's own registry resolution re-checks the recorded policy against the code it loaded and refuses by name before anything is built or signed.

decisions.text: One application value, a mode that picks its pin. applicationIn builds the value for a mode; the open value stays the constant every other module names, and the closed value differs from it in the pin title alone. The negative host, the conformance driver and the entry commands keep using the open constant.

The loader carries the mode. For a registry read as closed, the commands insert, terminate, fold and inspect run with the environment whose release loader ignores the application it is asked for and loads the mode's. An open registry runs with the unchanged environment, so nothing about an open run changes, not even a closure.

The mode read is one read of one output. It opens the provider the command names, finds the state output by its token, takes the recorded application policy, and compares it with the policy each mode's code gives for this registry identity. The open code is required; the closed code is optional, so an older blueprint with no closed title still reads an open registry.
The refusal of an update names the registry. It is raised through the same failure path every refusal takes, so the receipt, the trace and the exit status are the ones of any client refusal.
--closed is split out before the shared tokenizer and carried as the create command's first field. It is refused by name on every other command.

modules-data-and-functions.text: No new library module. The test suite gains one module.
Data. Names only; fields as named.

Constraints. modeTitle is injective. applicationIn Open equals the constant value of today. applicationIn Closed equals it in every field but the pin. modeOfRecordedPolicy is total and never chooses a mode whose derivation is absent or unequal. registryMode writes nothing and opens no wallet.

order-of-work.text: One slice, in this order. Each step leaves the tree green for the jobs it can reach.
Add the mode and the closed value to Value.hs; keep the open constant.
Add the --closed split, the create field and the refusal to Command.hs, fix the pattern sites in the specs, and add the switch to the usage text.
Add the mode read, the following environment and the update refusal to Run.hs, and make create, fold and inspect use the mode's value.
Write ClosedModeSpec and register it with its tags; run the open-datum suite.
Add the --closed row to the settings table of docs/singular-node.md and a paragraph to onchain-release/DEMO1.md; regenerate their speech and, for the site page, its narration clips.
Run the cheap local legs below, fold fixes into the one code patch, and hand the candidate over for review.
The pull request is a stacked patch series: one patch for these pages, one for the code, one for the documentation. No journey commits are pushed.

invariants-and-what-makes-them-fail.text: Invariants and what makes them fail.
Each name is stable and appears in the tasks.

hosted-checks-that-accept-the-work.text: Hosted checks that accept the work.

The gate is the continuous integration itself: each row names the job and the verbatim command. The local leg is the cheap command run before the push; the hosted jobs run once on the pushed head, and no hosted job is repeated locally. The synthesis of the independent gate table and the plan author's table, with the cited red runs, is kept in the ticket's runtime record; the frozen result is below.

Every other required context that reads the open-datum commands, the archive or the registry (the recovery lanes, the Demo 1 refusal and two-actor jobs, the conformance devnet jobs and the devnet end-to-end parts) is listed in the runtime record's census and must be green on the exact head. The checks the author of the change runs before the push, outside the repository, are: the diff names only files of the touch list; no fenced file changed; no attribution in the pushed range; the effect-site records name the new test module's recording cell and nothing else; and the final tree equals the last approved checkpoint tree.

risks-the-plan-settles.text: A read before every command but create. Each later command now reads the state output once before it reads it again. A rig that counts or orders reads, and a journey that asserts on reads, could notice. The mode read is made through the same read path as any read, writes nothing, and a failure of it changes nothing; the hosted jobs that run these commands are the net.

The title in the value the entry commands pass. The entry commands pass the open value when closed code is loaded. This is correct because the title is read only by the loader, which the dispatch replaces, and it is guarded by a test that resolves a closed registry through that value.
An interrupted create has no state output. The mode read names it as a missing state, the command then runs as open-datum, and inspect prints its own refusal as today.

Help text read by the flags check. The check treats every --flag in the help's prose as unattributed. The explanation of the switch therefore says "the closed switch" and names --closed only on the create usage lines.

residuals-this-change-leaves-written-bef.text: Residuals this change leaves, written before the work.
The real blueprint's closed-datum title is first used by the devnet journey from the release archive, the next ticket of issue 650. Until then the title is proved requested, not proved present.
The write-once rule has no Lean statement, by ruling.
The node's refusal of a crafted update on a closed registry is the last ticket of issue 650.
singular registry describe on a closed registry is exercised by the journey ticket.

No hosted check asserts that the run page carries the closed line, or that the run page's speech is current: the presentation check does not name that folder. The flags check binds an invocation on the page to the help, the speech is regenerated with the extraction tool in the same change, and the acceptance walk reads the line. This is a missing job, reported to the epic owner.
